newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may tender Far North diamond field.
newsitem.headline: Russia may tender Far North diamond field.

text.p: The Russian government has set up a commission to decide whether to hold an international investment tender to develop the Lomonosov diamond field in the Far North, a senior local diamond official said on Tuesday.

"The government has made a good step which will allow us to sort out the financial, industrial and ecological questions of the project and probably to start mining soon," said the official, speaking from the icy Arkhangelsk region, where the Lomonosov mine is located.
Interfax news agency quoted local officials as saying several foreign firms, including South Africa's De Beers diamond group and Britain's RTZ Corp PLC, had expressed interest.
The Lomonosov project, initially to have started three years ago and to have been run by Russia's tiny Severalmaz diamond producing firm, was delayed by a lack of cash.
The official said the commission could decide to tender the field to a Russian company.
Interfax said Severalmaz had roughly estimated Lomonosov's reserves as having a market value of around $12 billion.
"The only thing we know now is that we have a big diamond field and that mining it is going to be profitable," the Arkhangelsk official said.
